content: Protein 2 is encoded by the EPB42 gene in humans. This protein is a cytoskeletal component specifically found in red blood cells. It functions as an ATP-binding protein and is believed to regulate the interaction between band 3 and ankyrin, two critical components of the red blood cell membrane. Protein 2 likely plays a significant role in maintaining the shape of erythrocytes and regulating their mechanical properties. Mutations in the EPB42 gene are associated with recessive spherocytic elliptocytosis and recessively inherited hereditary hemolytic anemia.
